title: Order ticket UI
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7) closes the execution loop. E29 gives us the OMS core and order state machine, E27 the accounts and key vault, E28 the per-account profiles and trade groups, E39 the risk caps and kill-switch. **E30 is the surface the human touches**: the order ticket.

The roadmap scopes this Epic as: "Market / limit / conditional entry; qty by contracts, notional, % equity, or risk-based from the SL distance; price stepping honouring `priceFilter`/`lotSizeFilter`; post-only, reduce-only, IOC/FOK/GTC; TP/SL attachment with tpslMode Full/Partial; account/trade-group selector with the fan-out preview; **arm/lock control plus an always-visible environment badge â€” no trading control is operable unless both are visible**; hotkeys; confirmation policy configurable per environment (demo may skip, live may not)" (30-release-roadmap.md Â§7.2, 34 pts, S16â€“S17).

Two product properties are load-bearing and are the reason this Epic exists as its own Epic rather than as UI bolted onto E29:
1. **Nothing fires by accident.** One-click trading is off by default, is armed through `POST /api/v1/settings/arm` for a bounded TTL, auto-disarms on inactivity/lock/env-switch/disconnect, and the environment (DEMO/LIVE) is restated on every trading surface and in every confirmation (US-ORD-005, SCR-075, CMP-229, CMP-139).
2. **Nothing goes out unprotected.** The mandatory native exchange-side stop-loss (owner decision, `20-architecture.md` P4) is expressed in the ticket as a field that cannot be emptied, and the backend rejects `native_stop_required` if it ever is (US-ORD-013, CMP-119, CMP-158).

Backend module: **M23** (API/WS Gateway â€” the ticket's REST/WS contract surface); consumes M14 (OMS) via `POST /api/v1/orders`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `GET /api/v1/risk/summary`, and the `orders`, `executions`, `positions`, `wallet`, `ticker.{symbol}` WS topics. Story domain: **ORD**.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (11-user-stories.md Â§17 ORD):** US-ORD-001 (order ticket, Must), US-ORD-002 (order types and flags, Must), US-ORD-003 (quantity presets and size ladder, Must), US-ORD-004 (risk-based sizing, Must), US-ORD-005 (one-click arm/lock, Must), US-ORD-006 (trading hotkeys, Must), US-ORD-012 (order templates, Should), US-ORD-013 (mandatory native SL â€” ticket-side expression, Must), US-ORD-014 (pre-trade risk preview, Should).
US-ORD-007..011 (chart/DOM click-trade, drag, cancel-from-chart, flatten, reverse) belong to **E31**; the backend enforcement of US-ORD-013 belongs to **E32**; group construction/fan-out execution belongs to **E28/E34**. This Epic owns the *ticket surface* and its client-side guarantees only.

**Screens:** SCR-060 (order ticket panel, single account), SCR-076 (order confirmation modal), SCR-077 (order rejection detail drawer), SCR-114 (trading defaults settings), SCR-113 (hotkey editor â€” trading-action rows), SCR-158 (rate-limited state), SCR-075 (demo/live banner & per-panel badges â€” consumption), SCR-061 (trade-group ticket â€” the account/group selector + fan-out preview slice only; group management is E28).

**Components:** CMP-100 PriceInput, CMP-101 QtyInput, CMP-102 SideToggle, CMP-103 OrderTypeTabs, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-107 OrderTicket, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-231 TifSelect, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal.

**API:** `POST /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}/ticker`, `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate`, `GET /api/v1/risk/summary`, `POST /api/v1/settings/arm`, `GET|PUT /api/v1/settings`, `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*`.
**WS topics:** `orders.{accountId}`, `executions.{accountId}`, `positions.{accountId}`, `wallet.{accountId}`, `ticker.{symbol}`.
**DB:** `hotkey_profiles` (existing, `0011_workspace`); user trading defaults and order templates ride the existing user-settings store â€” no new migration is introduced by this Epic beyond the templates column/table added in E30-S07.

**Children:** 7 Stories, 3 Tasks/Chore, 1 Spike (**34 engineering pts**), 7 Design tickets (23 pts), 6 QA tickets (22 pts), 3 Security tickets (8 pts).

### Estimate reconciliation (single number: 34)
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 budgets **34 pts** for E30 across S16–S17. That budget is the *engineering* capacity line, and this Epic reconciles to it exactly:

| Bucket | Keys | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering (Stories, Tasks, Spike) | E30-K01, E30-T01..T03, E30-S01..S07 | **34** |
| Design (design-discipline capacity, S13–S18) | E30-D01..D07 | 23 |
| QA (test-discipline capacity, S16–S18) | E30-Q01..Q06 | 22 |
| Security (security-discipline capacity, S15–S18) | E30-X01..X03 | 8 |

The Epic ticket's own `estimate` field is **34** — identical to the roadmap figure and to the rollup of its engineering children, so roadmap capacity planning, the Epic field and the child rollup are one number. Design, QA and Security children are *not* rolled into that number: they draw on their own discipline capacity (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA and QA/security sign-off mandatory companion work, not engineering scope) and several of them land outside the S16–S17 engineering window (S13–S15 design, S18 sign-off). No scope was added beyond the roadmap §7.2 sentence for this Epic; the S16–S17 engineering plan is K01 (1) + T01 (5) + S01 (5) + S02 (2) + S03 (5) + S04 (5) + S05 (2) + S06 (5) + S07 (2) + T02 (1) + T03 (1) = **34**.

## Out of scope
- Chart click-to-trade, order-line dragging, DOM ladder click-trade, flatten/reverse buttons (E31).
- Bracket child management, scaled ladders, break-even automation, trailing translation (E32); emulated OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase builders SCR-065..069 (E33).
- Trade-group CRUD, per-account enable/disable, fan-out execution and partial-failure unwind (E28/E34).
- Server-side native-SL invariant enforcement, risk-cap evaluation, kill-switch engine (E32/E39) â€” the ticket *consumes* and *displays* these.
- Positions/orders blotter SCR-063 (E29). Journal capture (E41). Live environment enablement (E44).
- Android / any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A complete demo order from the ticket
  Given a signed-in owner on the demo environment with account "Main" selected on SCR-060
  When they set limit buy 0.25 BTCUSDT at a valid tick price with the profile's stop attached and confirm
  Then POST /api/v1/orders returns 202, the ticket shows submitting -> accepted within 500 ms p95
  And the resulting order appears from the orders WS topic, not from the REST body alone
Scenario: No trading control is operable without arm state and environment both visible
  Given the environment badge or the arm state cannot be rendered for any reason
  Then every submit affordance on SCR-060 and SCR-061 is disabled with a stated reason
  And no order request can be issued by keyboard, hotkey or programmatic click
Scenario: The mandatory native stop cannot be removed
  Given an entry order on an account whose profile requires a native SL
  When the user clears the stop-loss field
  Then submit is blocked client-side with "This account requires a stop-loss on every order."
  And a crafted request omitting stop_loss is rejected server-side with native_stop_required
```

## Technical notes / design
Frontend package layout: `apps/web/src/features/order-ticket/` with a framework-free `packages/order-ticket-core` holding the pure validation/sizing/preview reducer so that the same code runs in unit tests, in Storybook and (as a parity fixture) against the backend's `24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 sizing algorithm. Client-side sizing is advisory: the server recomputes and rejects a mismatch beyond one lot (US-ORD-004 NFR).

Submit path: `Idempotency-Key` is REQUIRED on `POST /api/v1/orders`; the client derives one per user-intent (not per retry) so a retried submit can never double-place. One-click submissions additionally carry the `arm_token` from `POST /api/v1/settings/arm`. Response `202` returns a `TradeGroup` (single orders are one-leg groups server-side) â€” the UI must treat it as *acceptance*, and resolve terminal state from the `orders`/`executions` WS topics, showing "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" after 2 s.

Error codes surfaced by name, never by raw string matching: `validation_failed`/`native_stop_required`, `tick_size_violation`, `lot_size_violation`, `risk_limit_breached`, `trading_disabled` (kill-switch), `429` rate-limited (SCR-158), `502` exchange error (SCR-077 with verbatim retCode/retMsg from `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`).

## Test plan
Per-child test plans roll up to: unit â‰¥80% on `apps/web` and â‰¥85% on `packages/order-ticket-core`; contract tests against `22-api-openapi.yaml` for every request shape the ticket emits; a **sizing-parity** test that runs the same fixture matrix through the TS core and the Python `Â§9.3` implementation and asserts identical results; Playwright E2E on demo covering keyboard-only placement, arm/disarm, rejection, rate-limit and confirmation policy; perf harness asserting â‰¤8 ms recompute and â‰¤500 ms p95 clickâ†’ack; chaos: WS drop between ack and fill, kill-switch engaged mid-ticket, stale wallet.

## Security notes
Threats (04-security-program.md): accidental or induced order placement (arm bypass, clickjacking, hotkey while unfocused), privilege escalation through the account selector (manager selecting an ungranted account), leakage of exchange credentials or raw signatures in the rejection drawer, idempotency-key reuse causing double submission, and confirmation-policy tampering to disable LIVE confirmation. Controls: server-side scope resolution on every account id, `arm_token` validated server-side and invalidated on disarm/kill-switch/risk breach, redaction in `OrderDiagnostics`, audited `order.submitted`/`order.rejected`/`order.arm_toggled`/`trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled`. Data classification: financial + account-scoped; no secrets ever rendered.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The ticket is a form with a fieldset per section; the submit button's accessible name restates the full intent; errors are summarised at the top and linked to fields; the arm state is announced assertively on change and on auto-disarm; every hotkey has a visible, focusable equivalent; nothing (buy/sell, armed/locked, demo/live) is conveyed by colour alone.

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2): order submit â†’ ack p95 <300 ms on demo, of which â‰¤50 ms is backend-added â€” this Epic owns the client portion and must not add more than 20 ms between the user gesture and the request leaving the client. SCR-060 requires every input to recompute risk/fee/margin in â‰¤8 ms. Hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms client-side (US-ORD-006). Preview recompute â‰¤100 ms (US-ORD-014).

## Observability
Audit: `orders.submit` (source=ticket|hotkey|template), `orders.cancel`, `order.arm_toggled`, `trading_defaults.changed`, `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`. Analytics: `ticket.sizing_rule_used`, `order.confirmation_shown`, `order.confirmation_cancelled`, `order.rejection_viewed`, `order.blocked_ratelimited`. Client metrics: `cv_ticket_recompute_ms`, `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms` (histogram, env label), `cv_ticket_arm_state_seconds`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic AC verified end to end on demo: place â†’ reject â†’ correct â†’ place â†’ fill, from the ticket alone.
- [ ] Coverage: â‰¥80% `apps/web`, â‰¥85% `packages/order-ticket-core`; no package baseline regression.
- [ ] Docs reconciled: SCR-060/061/076/077/113/114/158 and CMP-100..232 entries match the shipped UI; `22-api-openapi.yaml` unchanged or amended by PR.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on every touched screen + a manual NVDA pass on placement, arming and rejection.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 client portion, the 8 ms recompute and the 50 ms hotkey budget all measured and recorded.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, all Critical/High closed, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] design: D-tickets Done â‰¥2 sprints before their consuming Story; design QA (E30-D07) closed.
- [ ] QA sign-off (E30-Q06) recorded; zero open P0/P1 against this Epic.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at the S17 Sprint Review (roadmap key date 2027-01-21: "first end-to-end demo trade").

## Dependencies
- **E29** OMS core & order state machine â€” `POST /api/v1/orders`, the order state machine, the `orders`/`executions` WS topics. Nothing in this Epic can submit before it exists.
- **E28** Per-account profiles & trade groups â€” profile limits, sizing rule, SL/TP offsets, `POST /trade-groups/preview`.
- **E27** Accounts & key vault â€” account list, wallet snapshot, per-account health.
- **E39** Risk caps, lockouts & kill-switch â€” `GET /risk/summary`, `trading_disabled`, lockout states shown on the ticket.
- **E09** Auth/RBAC â€” account scoping, step-up for dangerous settings. **E17** WS transport. **E13/E10** design system + app shell for CMP primitives.
- Consumers: **E31** (chart/DOM trading reuses the ticket's intent layer, arm state and confirmation policy), **E33** (algo builders embed the ticket's sizing and bracket blocks), **E41** (journal reads `source=ticket`).

## Branch
`feat/e30-order-ticket-epic` as the umbrella name; one branch and PR per child ticket (`feat/e30-<short>`), â‰¤400 LOC diff preferred.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Measure order-path latency: recompute, click-to-request and hotkey
body:
## Context
Three client-side numbers gate this Epic and none of them has been measured yet on the real app shell:
1. SCR-060 requires **every input to recompute risk/fee/margin in â‰¤8 ms** (pure client-side).
2. Budget #4 (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2) allows **p95 <300 ms clickâ†’ack on demo**, of which â‰¤50 ms is backend-added and ~250 ms is Bybit demo REST RTT â€” leaving almost nothing for the client. We must know what the gestureâ†’`fetch()` portion actually costs inside the Electron shell with a live workspace (chart + footprint + ladder) already consuming frame budget.
3. US-ORD-006 requires **hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms client-side**.

If the ticket cannot hit these while sharing a renderer with the WebGL chart engine, the architecture must change *before* E30-T01 is written â€” e.g. moving the sizing reducer into a worker, or decoupling the submit path from React's render cycle with a direct imperative dispatch. That is exactly what this spike decides.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. This spike is explicitly **not expected to produce production-shippable code**; the harness it builds may be promoted into E30-Q03.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A throwaway harness on `spike/e30-ticket-latency` mounting a stub of CMP-107 OrderTicket inside the real app shell (SCR-010) with a chart panel (SCR-030) and a DOM ladder panel (SCR-050) live on demo data, so the measurement includes realistic main-thread contention.
- Measure, with `performance.mark`/`measure` and 1 000 samples each: (a) full ticket recompute after a price keystroke, a qty keystroke and a sizing-mode switch; (b) gestureâ†’`fetch()` dispatch for pointer click, `Ctrl+Enter` and a bound hotkey; (c) WS `orders` event â†’ rendered state transition.
- Compare three reducer placements: synchronous in the React event handler, in a `useSyncExternalStore` store outside React rendering, and in a worker with a structured-clone hop.
- Record results against the three budgets in a comparison table on the ticket and in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.

## Out of scope
Backend latency (E29 measures its own â‰¤50 ms), Bybit RTT, production styling, real order submission (the harness posts to a local stub).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The three budgets are answered with numbers
  When the spike closes
  Then p50/p95/p99 are recorded for recompute, click->dispatch and hotkey->dispatch under a loaded workspace
  And each is stated as PASS or FAIL against 8 ms, the budget #4 client allowance and 50 ms
Scenario: A decision follows from the numbers
  Given recompute p95 exceeds 8 ms in the synchronous-React placement
  Then the ADR records the store-outside-React or worker placement as the mandated design for E30-T01
Scenario: A failing result escalates rather than being absorbed
  Given no placement meets the hotkey budget under a loaded workspace
  Then a risk entry is added to docs/plan/32-risk-register.md and the Architect is asked for a scope decision before S16 planning closes
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure with the chart engine actually rendering (E11/E12 build), not a blank page â€” main-thread contention is the whole point. Use `chrome://tracing` / Electron's tracing to attribute time between React reconciliation, layout and the reducer itself. For the worker variant, measure the structured-clone cost of the `OrderDraft` + `Instrument` + `Wallet` snapshot payload, which is the dominant term at this size.

Sampling method: 1 000 synthetic keystrokes via `dispatchEvent` on the focused input at 20 Hz (a realistic fast-typing rate), interleaved with live WS traffic at the reference workspace rate from `23-ws-protocol.md` Â§16.3. Report p50/p95/p99 and the worst 1% tail, not the mean.

## Test plan
The harness is itself the test. Reproducibility: the run script is checked into the spike branch with a fixed synthetic-input seed; two independent runs must agree within 15% at p95 or the measurement is rejected as noisy and repeated on a quiet machine.

## Security notes
The harness must not hold a real API key or submit to a real exchange endpoint; it posts to a local stub only. No credentials on the spike branch (secret scanning applies to spike branches too).

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” throwaway measurement harness with no shipped UI. The a11y properties of the real ticket are covered by E30-D05 and E30-Q05.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance work. Budgets under test: 8 ms recompute (SCR-060), budget #4 client portion (Â§5.2), 50 ms hotkeyâ†’submit (US-ORD-006 NFR).

## Observability
The chosen instrumentation (`cv_ticket_recompute_ms`, `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms`) is prototyped here and promoted into E30-T01 so the budgets stay measurable in production, not only in the spike.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Comparison table with p50/p95/p99 for all three placements recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] ADR written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the chosen reducer placement (even if the decision is "synchronous is fine").
- [ ] E30-T01 updated with the mandated design before it starts.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a budget cannot be met.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; branch left unmerged and archived.

## Dependencies
- **E29** â€” the `/orders` request shape being dispatched (a stub is acceptable if E29's contract is merged).
- **E13** app shell / design system and **E11/E12** chart engine build, to reproduce realistic main-thread load.

## Branch
`spike/e30-ticket-latency` (throwaway, never merged). PR: none; findings posted on the ticket.

## References

title: Build packages/order-ticket-core: draft, validation, sizing, submit
body:
## Context
Every ticket surface in the product â€” SCR-060 single-account ticket, SCR-061 group ticket, E31's chart and DOM click-trade, E33's algo builders â€” must produce an identical, identically-validated order draft. If that logic lives in React components it will be duplicated and will drift, and a drift here is a mis-sized order with real money behind it.

This Task creates **`packages/order-ticket-core`**: a framework-free TypeScript package holding the order draft model, the validation rules, the client-side sizing reducer and the submit pipeline. It is pure (no DOM, no fetch, no React) apart from an injected transport port, so it is unit-testable exhaustively and can be run in a worker if E30-K01 mandates that placement.

The sizing reducer is a **mirror of the backend algorithm** in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 (sizing), Â§9.3.1 (stop resolution), Â§9.3.2 (clamp order) and Â§9.3.3 (take-profit resolution). It is advisory: the server recomputes and rejects a mismatch beyond one lot (US-ORD-004 NFR). The parity test in the Test plan is what keeps the mirror honest.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/order-ticket-core/src/model.ts` â€” `OrderDraft`, `SizingSpec` (`fixed_qty` | `fixed_notional` | `pct_equity` | `risk_based` | `profile`), `StopSpec`/`TpSpec` (`ticks` | `percent` | `atr` | `r_multiple`), `TicketContext` (`Instrument`, `AccountProfile`, `Wallet`, `Ticker`, `RiskSummary`, `env`, `armState`).
- `validate.ts` â€” the full rule set from SCR-060 "Validation & messages": tick multiple, min qty, qty step, min notional, leverage â‰¤ profile cap, SL/TP side correctness, reduce-only requires an open position, post-only would-cross detection, insufficient margin, **mandatory native SL when the profile requires it**, symbol not allowed, lockout/kill-switch engaged. Each rule returns a stable `code` plus the exact human copy from SCR-060 â€” copy lives in one place, not in components.
- `size.ts` â€” the Â§9.3 mirror including the Â§9.3.2 clamp chain in its fixed order, returning `{qty, appliedClamps[], stop, tps, warnings}` so the UI can say "reduced from 1.2 to 0.8 by max_position_notional".
- `submit.ts` â€” the submit pipeline: build `PlaceOrderRequest`, derive the `Idempotency-Key` **per user intent** (stable across retries of the same intent, fresh for a new intent), attach `arm_token` for one-click submissions, POST via the injected transport, map `202` to an optimistic `TradeGroup` view, and resolve terminal state from the `orders`/`executions` WS topics with a 2 s "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" fallback.
- `errors.ts` â€” mapping from backend error codes (`validation_failed`/`native_stop_required`, `tick_size_violation`, `lot_size_violation`, `risk_limit_breached`, `trading_disabled`, `429`, `502`) to UI presentation intent (inline field / banner / SCR-077 drawer / SCR-158 state).
- Instrumentation hooks `cv_ticket_recompute_ms` and `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms`, in the placement chosen by E30-K01.

## Out of scope
Any React component (E30-S01+), the confirmation modal, network retry policy beyond idempotent replay, backend enforcement of any rule (E29/E32/E39 own that â€” this package is defence in depth, never the only check).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sizing parity with the backend
  Given the shared fixture matrix of instruments, profiles, wallets and stop specs
  When each fixture is sized by packages/order-ticket-core and by the backend Â§9.3 implementation
  Then the resulting qty, applied clamps and resolved stop are identical for every fixture
Scenario: Idempotency key is stable per intent
  Given a submit that fails with a network error and is retried by the user without changing any field
  Then the same Idempotency-Key is sent and the server replays rather than double-placing
  And changing any field before retrying produces a new key
Scenario: Clamp explanation is preserved
  Given a requested size of 1.2 that max_position_notional reduces to 0.8
  Then the result reports qty 0.8 with appliedClamps naming max_position_notional in the Â§9.3.2 order
Scenario: A missing native stop is a hard validation failure
  Given a profile with require_native_stop and a draft with no stop
  Then validate() returns code native_stop_required and submit() refuses to build a request at all
```

## Technical notes / design
```ts
export interface TicketCore {
  size(draft: OrderDraft, ctx: TicketContext): SizingResult;
  validate(draft: OrderDraft, ctx: TicketContext): ValidationResult; // ordered, all failures returned
  buildRequest(draft: OrderDraft, ctx: TicketContext): PlaceOrderRequest;
  submit(req: PlaceOrderRequest, ports: { post: PostOrder; clock: Clock }): Promise<SubmitOutcome>;
}
```
`validate()` returns **all** failures (the SCR-060 a11y contract summarises errors at the top), ordered by field position. Stop resolution follows Â§9.3.1 exactly, including conservative rounding *away* from entry so realised risk never exceeds the budget, and the `stop_fallback` flag when ATR is still in warmup.

Config keys: `CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 2000, the reconciling threshold), `CV_TICKET_PREVIEW_DEBOUNCE_MS` (default 80, used by E30-S06's `/trade-groups/preview` calls).

Decimal arithmetic only â€” all prices and quantities are strings parsed into a decimal type (never JS `number`) before arithmetic, because tick/lot multiples must be exact; a float rounding error here becomes a `tick_size_violation` at the exchange.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥85%)**: validation matrix â€” every rule Ã— pass/fail; tick and lot rounding across at least four instruments with different filters; each sizing mode; the full clamp chain in order including two clamps binding at once; stop resolution for ticks/percent/atr with ATR warmup fallback; TP ladder remainder absorption (Â§9.3.3); idempotency-key derivation stability and change detection; error-code mapping exhaustiveness (a test fails if a new backend code has no mapping).
- **Parity**: the shared fixture matrix run against the backend implementation in CI as a required check (`ticket_sizing_parity`).
- **Property**: for random valid inputs, the sized qty is always a lot multiple, never exceeds any clamp, and the resolved stop is always on the correct side of entry.
- **Contract**: every `buildRequest()` output validates against `PlaceOrderRequest` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/instruments/{BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT,1000PEPEUSDT}.json` from `GET /instruments/{symbol}`; `fixtures/profiles/*.json` per Â§9.2.

## Security notes
The package never touches credentials â€” it receives an injected transport. The `arm_token` is passed through, never stored in the package or persisted. Idempotency-key derivation must not be predictable from another user's session (derive from a session-scoped random seed plus the intent hash, not from the intent hash alone) so a third party cannot force a replay collision.

## Accessibility notes
N/A directly (no UI), but the package owns the **error copy** that the a11y error summary renders; each message must be a complete sentence naming the constraint and the fix, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`, and is reviewed as part of E30-D05.

## Performance notes
`size()` + `validate()` together must run in â‰¤8 ms p95 under the loaded-workspace conditions measured in E30-K01, benchmarked in CI with a regression gate at +20%.

## Observability
`cv_ticket_recompute_ms` (histogram), `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms` (histogram, `env` label), `cv_ticket_validation_failed_total{code}`. No PII or account ids in metric labels.

- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by the named tests; parity check green as a required CI check.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥85% on the package.

title: Build SCR-060 order ticket with entry types and all order flags
body:
## Context
US-ORD-001 (Must) and US-ORD-002 (Must) are the heart of the product's execution loop: "a fast order ticket with type, side, size, price and target accounts, so that I can submit precisely" and "market, limit, stop, stop-limit and conditional orders with TIF, reduce-only, post-only and close-on-trigger, so that I can express any intent".

This Story builds the **SCR-060 Order ticket panel (single account)** shell and its order-type/flag surface, composing the design-system trading components onto `packages/order-ticket-core` (E30-T01). Sizing modes are E30-S02/S03, arm/confirm is E30-S04, the preview and group selector are E30-S06 â€” this Story ships the panel, the type/side/price fields, the flags, and the submit path with a fixed quantity.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-001, US-ORD-002.** Screen **SCR-060**.
- `apps/web/src/features/order-ticket/OrderTicketPanel.tsx` composing **CMP-107 OrderTicket** from **CMP-102 SideToggle**, **CMP-103 OrderTypeTabs** (Market / Limit / Conditional; emulated types rendered with the visible "(emulated)" badge but disabled until E33), **CMP-100 PriceInput** (tick-aware, with the "(rounded to nearest tick)" caption), **CMP-101 QtyInput** in `qty` mode, **CMP-231 TifSelect** (GTC/IOC/FOK/PostOnly with per-order-type availability and a stated reason when unavailable), **CMP-119 BracketEditor**, **CMP-232 LimitsChip**, **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal**.
- Flags: `reduce_only`, `post_only` (via TIF `PostOnly`), `close_on_trigger`; conditional orders with `trigger.price`, `trigger_by` (`LastPrice`/`MarkPrice`/`IndexPrice`) and `direction` (`rise`/`fall`).
- Price helpers: `Alt+B`/`Alt+A` snap to bid/ask, `Alt+M` mid, sourced from WS `ticker.{symbol}` (`23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14.8).
- Data wiring: `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` (tick, lot, min notional, leverage), `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, WS `wallet.{accountId}`, WS `ticker.{symbol}`; submit `POST /api/v1/orders`; terminal state from WS `orders.{accountId}` / `executions.{accountId}`.
- All SCR-060 states: ready Â· validating Â· submitting (button becomes a progress state, duplicate submits blocked) Â· accepted Â· rejected (inline, with the exchange code and the plain-language explanation) Â· blocked-by-profile Â· blocked-by-lockout Â· frozen Â· disconnected Â· pending-key.
- Storybook stories for every state and every order type; `CMP-107` Storybook entries Market, Limit, Conditional, Rejected, RateLimited.

## Out of scope
Sizing modes beyond explicit qty (E30-S02/S03), arm/lock and the confirmation modal (E30-S04), hotkeys (E30-S05), risk preview and the account/group selector (E30-S06), templates and trading defaults (E30-S07), the rejection drawer and rate-limited banner (E30-T02), chart/DOM entry (E31).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit order (US-ORD-001)
  Given BTCUSDT, account "Main", one-click disarmed, demo environment
  When I enter a limit buy of 0.1 at 63000 with the profile's stop attached and confirm
  Then the order is validated client-side, POST /api/v1/orders returns 202
  And an acknowledgement carrying the exchange order id appears within 500 ms
Scenario: Validation failure before any exchange call (US-ORD-001)
  Given a quantity of 0.0004 on an instrument whose minimum is 0.001
  When I press submit
  Then submission is blocked before any network call with the field-level message "Minimum 0.001, step 0.001."
  And the message names the constraint and the field is focusable from the error summary
Scenario: Conditional order (US-ORD-002)
  When I set trigger price 63400, trigger source Mark and direction rise
  Then the conditional order is created and displayed as untriggered with its trigger conditions restated
Scenario: Post-only rejection (US-ORD-002)
  Given time-in-force PostOnly and a limit price that would cross the spread
  Then the client warns before sending, and if the exchange still rejects, the rejection is shown verbatim with a "reprice" suggestion and my inputs are retained
Scenario: Reduce-only guard (US-ORD-002)
  Given no open position on the selected account and symbol
  When I check reduce-only
  Then submission is blocked client-side with "Reduce-only needs an open position." and the request is never issued
Scenario: Exchange rejection retains context (US-ORD-001)
  Given the exchange rejects the order with retCode 110007
  Then the ticket shows the exchange message and code, keeps every input, and the attempt is journaled and audited as order.rejected
```

## Technical notes / design
All validation and request building come from `packages/order-ticket-core` â€” this Story contains **no** arithmetic and no copy strings of its own. Components are pure and driven by a single `useSyncExternalStore` ticket store (or the worker placement, per E30-K01/ADR), so a WS `ticker` update at 100 ms cadence never re-renders the whole panel.

Submit is optimistic: on `202` the panel enters `accepted` with the returned one-leg `TradeGroup`, then reconciles against `orders.{accountId}`; if no matching event arrives within `CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 000 ms) the state becomes "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" rather than a false "filled". Duplicate submits are blocked by disabling the button *and* by the idempotency key, not by the button alone.

Emulated order types appear in CMP-103 with the "(emulated)" badge per the safety-transparency rule but are `disabled` with `disabledReason="Available from the algo builders (coming in E33)"` â€” never silently absent.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: state machine of the panel (readyâ†’validatingâ†’submittingâ†’accepted/rejected); flag availability matrix per order type; trigger-field visibility; price-helper snapping; duplicate-submit suppression.
- **Contract**: the emitted `PlaceOrderRequest` validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` for market, limit, conditional and each flag combination.
- **Integration**: against a recorded demo fixture set â€” accepted, rejected (`110007` post-only would cross), `422` native_stop_required, `403` account scope.
- **E2E (Playwright, demo)**: keyboard-only limit order placement end to end; covered in E30-Q02.
- **Visual + axe**: every Storybook state.
- Coverage target â‰¥80% frontend.

## Security notes
The account id used on submit is taken from the selector state but is **always** re-authorised server-side (`x-rbac: orders:write, scope: granted_accounts`); a Viewer sees the panel read-only with a lock notice and no submit affordance exists in the DOM at all (not merely disabled). Rejection display uses the mapped presentation from `order-ticket-core`; raw request payloads are only ever shown through `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` (E30-T02), which is redacted and audited on read.

## Accessibility notes
The panel is a `<form>` with a `<fieldset>` per section (side/type, price, quantity, brackets, flags). The submit button's accessible name restates the full intent: "Submit buy 0.25 BTCUSDT limit 64 010 with stop 63 900". Errors are summarised at the top of the form with links to the offending fields (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). The tick-rounding caption is `aria-live="polite"`. Unavailable TIF options are disabled **with a stated reason**. Buy/sell are labelled "Buy / Long" and "Sell / Short" in words, never colour alone. Full keyboard path verified: tab order, `Ctrl+Enter` submit, `Esc` clear.

## Performance notes
Every input recalculates risk/fee/margin in â‰¤8 ms (SCR-060). Client contribution to budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2, p95 <300 ms demo) â‰¤20 ms from gesture to request dispatch. WS `ticker` updates must not cause a full-panel re-render â€” asserted by a render-count test.

## Observability
Audit `orders.submit` `{account, source: "ticket", environment}`; `order.rejected` with the exchange code. Analytics `ticket.sizing_rule_used`. Metric `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms{env}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six Gherkin scenarios pass by automated test (unit/contract/integration) or a recorded QA step with an automation follow-up filed.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; no package baseline regression.
- [ ] SCR-060 entry in `14-screens-catalogue.md` matches the shipped panel; CMP-107 Storybook entries complete.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-060; manual screen-reader pass on placement and rejection.
- [ ] 8 ms recompute and â‰¤20 ms dispatch measured and recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: built panel compared against the E30-D06 handoff pack; discrepancies fixed or filed.
- [ ] Security review of the account-scope path; QA sign-off comment posted per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; feature flag `ff_order_ticket` recorded (demo on, live off).
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E30-T01** â€” validation, request building and the submit pipeline.
- **E30-D06** â€” the handoff pack must be Done â‰¥2 sprints earlier (S14) per the design-ahead rule.
- **E29** â€” `POST /api/v1/orders`, the order state machine and the `orders`/`executions` topics.

## Branch

## Context
US-ORD-003 (Must): "configurable size presets on buttons and number keys, so that sizing is one keystroke". The roadmap scope for this Epic requires "qty by contracts, notional, % equity, or risk-based from the SL distance" â€” this Story ships the first three modes plus the preset ladder; risk-based sizing has its own Story (E30-S03) because it couples to the stop and to the mandatory-SL invariant.

Presets are per symbol-class and per account profile, and the number-key mapping is remappable (US-ORD-003 NFR), which is why the binding lives in `hotkey_profiles` rather than in component state.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-003.** Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-114** (the preset ladder definition lives in Trading defaults; the editing UI itself is E30-S07 â€” this Story consumes the stored ladder).

- Disabled presets: a preset resolving below the instrument minimum renders disabled with the minimum stated in its accessible name and in visible text.
- Sizing-mode switch via **CMP-003 SegmentedControl** with `aria-describedby` explaining the active formula; the mode persists per symbol-class in user settings (`GET|PUT /api/v1/settings`).
- Clamp reporting: when `Â§9.3.2` clamps reduce the size, the reduction and its cause are shown inline ("reduced from 1.2 to 0.8 by max_position_notional").

## Out of scope
Risk-based sizing and the stop coupling (E30-S03); editing the preset ladder and defaults (E30-S07); the hotkey editor screen SCR-113 (E30-S05 wires the trading rows, E13/settings owns the screen); server-side sizing (E28 Â§9.3).

```gherkin
Scenario: Notional mode
  Given sizing mode "fixed notional" and 25 000 USDT with a mark price of 64 000

Scenario: Stale equity blocks equity-derived modes
  Given the wallet snapshot for the account is older than 2 s and cannot be refreshed
  Then % equity presets and % equity mode are disabled with "Account balance is stale" and fixed-qty sizing still works
```

- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: each sizing mode's rendering of the derived value; preset resolution incl. percent presets; disabled-preset condition; number-key activation and its suppression in text fields; stale-equity gating; clamp message rendering.

- **E2E**: preset â†’ submit path (in E30-Q02).

Presets are per user and contain no secrets. Each preset button's accessible name states the resolved quantity, not just the label ("0.1 BTC, 5 percent of equity"); disabled presets state why. The derived quantity is in an `aria-live="polite"` region so a screen-reader user hears the resolved size change when they switch mode or press a preset.

title: Ship risk-based sizing and the mandatory native stop-loss field in the ticket
body:
## Context
US-ORD-004 (Must): "size derived from my risk and stop distance, so that every trade risks what I intend". US-ORD-013 (Must): "every entry carries an exchange-side stop, so that my risk survives the app dying" â€” the product's **core safety invariant** (`docs/research/24-owner-decisions.md` cross-cutting Â§3, `20-architecture.md` principle P4).

These two ship together because they are the same control: the stop distance is simultaneously the risk denominator and the protective order. A ticket that lets you clear the stop is a ticket that lets you both trade unprotected and size meaninglessly.

The server is the enforcement point (`POST /api/v1/orders` rejects with `validation_failed` / `native_stop_required`, and E32 owns the OMS-side invariant). This Story is the *user-facing expression*: a field that cannot be emptied, a persistent non-dismissible notice, and a live risk read-out.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-004, US-ORD-013 (ticket surface).** Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-131** (read-only reference to the per-account requirement flag).
- **CMP-119 BracketEditor**: SL and TP in `ticks` / `%` / `R` units, `trigger_by` selector (Last/Mark/Index), `tpsl_mode` Full or Partial, and `nativeSlConfirmed` gating submit â€” submit is disabled until a native SL is present whenever the profile requires it.
- **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice** rendered persistently and non-dismissibly in the bracket section.
- **CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel**: risk in USDT and in R, implied risk % of equity, the resolved stop price and distance, recomputed on every stop or price change with the change visibly highlighted.
- Risk-based sizing mode in **CMP-101 QtyInput**: `riskPct` with a required `stopDistance`; quantity is derived, rounded to the lot step, and the implied risk restated after rounding (rounding down risk, never up).
- Opt-out surfacing: when the owner has disabled the invariant for an account, the ticket shows a persistent warning banner on that account and states that every order will be journaled as unprotected (US-ORD-013 scenario 3) â€” the ticket never offers the opt-out itself; it is set on SCR-131 by the owner.
- Attach-failure state: when the entry is accepted but the protective stop is not yet confirmed, the ticket shows the distinct **"order live, protective stop pending"** state required by `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2, non-colour-only.

## Out of scope
Server-side invariant enforcement and the retry/flatten policy on attach failure (E32); trailing-stop translation (E32); partial TP ladders beyond expressing `tpsl_mode` (E32/E33); profile editing (E28/SCR-131).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk sizing (US-ORD-004)
  Given risk 0.5% of a 20 000 USDT equity and a stop 120 USDT away from entry
  Then the quantity is computed, rounded to the lot step, and displayed together with the implied risk in USDT and in R
Scenario: Stop moved recomputes instantly (US-ORD-004)
  When I change the stop price
  Then the quantity and the implied risk recompute within 8 ms and the changed values are visibly highlighted
Scenario: No stop defined (US-ORD-004)
  Given risk-based sizing is selected and no stop is set
  Then submit is blocked with "Risk sizing requires a stop distance." and no request is issued
Scenario: The mandatory native stop cannot be cleared (US-ORD-013)
  Given an account whose profile requires a native stop-loss
  When I clear the stop-loss field
  Then submit is blocked with "This account requires a stop-loss on every order." and the SafetyInvariantNotice remains visible
Scenario: Server disagreement is fatal, not silent (US-ORD-004 NFR)
  Given the client-computed quantity differs from the server's recomputation by more than one lot
  Then the server rejects the order and the ticket shows the server's quantity and the discrepancy rather than retrying
Scenario: Protective stop pending (US-ORD-013)
  Given the entry is acknowledged but no exchange-side stop is confirmed yet
  Then the ticket shows a distinct "order live, protective stop pending" state in text and icon, not colour alone
  And a critical alert has been raised by the backend, which the ticket surfaces as a link
Scenario: Explicit opt-out is loud (US-ORD-013)
  Given the owner has disabled the invariant for this account
  Then a persistent warning banner names the account and states that orders are journaled as unprotected
```

## Technical notes / design
Stop resolution follows `24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3.1 exactly: `ticks` â†’ `ref Â± value*tick_size`; `percent` â†’ `ref*(1âˆ“value)`; `atr` â†’ `ref âˆ“ atr(period)*multiple`; `r_multiple` is invalid *for the stop itself* and is not offered as an SL unit. Rounding is conservative â€” the resolved stop moves **further** from entry, never closer, so realised risk never exceeds the budget. ATR warmup falls back to `fallback_sl_offset_pct` with a visible `stop_fallback` flag.

Risk-based quantity: `qty = floor((equity * riskPct) / stopDistancePerUnit / lotStep) * lotStep`, then the Â§9.3.2 clamp chain, then a restatement of the *post-rounding* risk (which is always â‰¤ the requested risk). All arithmetic is decimal, in `order-ticket-core`.

The "protective stop pending" state is driven by the backend's `NakedPositionAlert` path (`20-architecture.md` Â§10.2) observed on the `orders`/`positions` WS topics â€” the ticket never infers it from the absence of data, because absence is also what a WS gap looks like.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: risk formula across equity/stop/lot combinations incl. sub-lot results; conservative rounding direction; ATR fallback; "no stop" block; cleared-stop block; opt-out banner rendering; pending-stop state transitions.
- **Contract**: `stop_loss` spec serialisation for each unit against `PlaceOrderRequest`.
- **Integration**: server recomputation mismatch (>1 lot) surfaces the discrepancy; attach-failure fixture drives the pending state.
- **Safety suite**: a dedicated test asserts that **no** code path in the ticket can build a request without `stop_loss` when the profile requires it â€” this test is part of the R3 required-check safety suite (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4 Safety gate), so a failure blocks merge, not just release.
- **E2E** in E30-Q02; **chaos** (ack without stop confirmation) in E30-Q04.

## Security notes
This is a safety-critical surface and is `security`-labelled by default per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8. Abuse case: a crafted client request omitting `stop_loss`, or with a stop on the wrong side, must be rejected server-side (`native_stop_required`) â€” asserted in E30-X02, not assumed here. The opt-out must never be togglable from the ticket; a manual abuse-case check confirms the ticket exposes no such control and that a crafted profile-update request from a manager is refused.

## Accessibility notes
The stop and TP fields are in a labelled fieldset stating the unit; the SafetyInvariantNotice is `role="note"` and always in the accessibility tree. The risk read-out is `aria-live="polite"` and announces "risk 27.5 USDT, 0.8 percent of equity, 1 R" on change (throttled to at most one announcement per 500 ms so fast typing does not flood the screen reader). The "protective stop pending" state is `role="alert"` and is distinguishable in greyscale. The blocked-submit reason is announced when submit is attempted, not only rendered.

## Performance notes
Recompute on stop change â‰¤8 ms (SCR-060). The announcement throttle must not delay the visual update. Risk-read-out updates driven by `ticker` must not exceed one recompute per animation frame.

## Observability
Audit: `orders.submit` includes the resolved stop and the sizing mode; `order.blocked_native_sl_missing` (audited, high severity) when the invariant blocks a submit; `order.unprotected_submitted` when an opt-out account submits. Analytics `ticket.risk_sizing_used`, `ticket.stop_fallback_used`.

- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; CMP-119/CMP-121/CMP-158 Storybook states complete.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on the risk read-out and the pending-stop alert.

title: Implement arm/lock, the environment badge and confirmation policy
body:
## Context
US-ORD-005 (Must): "an explicit arm/lock toggle for one-click trading, so that I never fire an order by accident." The roadmap states this Epic's hardest constraint outright: **"arm/lock control plus an always-visible environment badge â€” no trading control is operable unless both are visible"** (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.2).

That sentence is an availability-of-the-guard requirement, not a styling note: if the arm state or the environment cannot be determined and displayed, trading must fail closed. This Story implements that, plus the per-environment confirmation policy â€” demo may skip confirmation, **live may not**.

Arming is server-backed: `POST /api/v1/settings/arm` returns an `arm_token` with a TTL (default 300 s, max 3600 s) that must accompany any order flagged `one_click`, and that the server invalidates on disarm, session end, kill-switch engagement or a risk-cap breach.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-005**, and the confirmation-policy half of **US-SET-003** as consumed by the ticket. Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-076** (order confirmation modal), **SCR-075** (demo/live banner and per-panel badges â€” consumption), **SCR-040** (arm-state display in the chart trading overlay settings â€” the shared arm store only).
- **CMP-229 ArmToggle** (`scope: "global"` here; chart/DOM scopes are E31), **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal**, **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard** wrapping every submit affordance, **CMP-044 ConfirmDialog** composing SCR-076 with **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip**, **CMP-232 LimitsChip**, **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice**.
- Arm lifecycle: `POST /api/v1/settings/arm {armed, ttl_seconds}` â†’ token held **in memory only, never persisted** (US-ORD-005 NFR: "state never persists across restarts"); auto-disarm on 30 min inactivity, session lock, environment switch, WS disconnect, kill-switch engagement, risk-cap lockout â€” each with the reason displayed.
- A persistent, high-visibility armed indicator naming the armed state, the target account(s) and the active size (US-ORD-005 scenario 2).
- Confirmation policy from user settings (`GET|PUT /api/v1/settings`, edited on SCR-114 by E30-S07): `always` / `live only` / `never when armed`; **"never" is unavailable for LIVE market orders** and the option is rendered disabled with the reason. SCR-076 restates environment, account(s), side, symbol, type, qty, price, brackets, estimated cost, resulting exposure and profile-limit results, with a configurable 20 s inactivity auto-cancel.
- Fail-closed guard: if `armState` or `environment` is `unknown` (store not hydrated, settings fetch failed, WS auth lost), every submit affordance is disabled with a stated reason and `CMP-139` refuses to dispatch.

## Out of scope
Chart/DOM arm scopes and their click-trade gating (E31); the kill-switch engine and risk lockout evaluation (E39); the environment switcher SCR-074 and live enablement (E44); editing the confirmation policy UI (E30-S07 builds SCR-114).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Disarmed by default (US-ORD-005)
  Given a brand-new session, including after an app restart
  Then one-click is locked and every order requires confirmation, regardless of what was armed before
Scenario: Arming is visible and specific (US-ORD-005)
  When I arm one-click
  Then a persistent high-visibility indicator states the armed state, the target account(s) and the active size
  And the server has issued an arm_token with a stated expiry shown in the indicator
Scenario: Auto-disarm states its reason (US-ORD-005)
  Given 30 minutes of inactivity, or a session lock, or an environment switch, or a WS disconnect
  Then one-click auto-disarms, the reason is displayed, and the arm_token is discarded client-side
Scenario: Fail closed when the guard cannot be shown
  Given the environment badge or the arm state cannot be resolved
  Then every submit affordance is disabled with a stated reason and no request can be dispatched by click, keyboard or hotkey
Scenario: Live cannot skip confirmation
  Given the live environment and a market order
  Then the "never confirm" policy is unavailable and disabled with a reason, and SCR-076 is shown with no default-focused confirm button
Scenario: Confirmation restates the whole order
  When the confirmation modal opens
  Then environment, account(s), side, symbol, type, quantity, price, brackets, estimated cost, resulting exposure and profile-limit results are all restated
  And the modal auto-cancels after the configured inactivity period without submitting
Scenario: Kill-switch invalidates arming immediately
  Given the kill-switch is engaged while one-click is armed
  Then the client disarms within one second of the WS event, the reason is announced, and a subsequent one-click submit is refused server-side with trading_disabled
```

## Technical notes / design
The arm state lives in a single app-wide store with three values: `locked`, `armed{token, expiresAt, scope}`, `unknown`. `unknown` is the initial value and is *also* the value on any error â€” there is no optimistic default. `CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard` is a wrapper, not a hook, so that no submit handler can exist outside it; a lint rule (`no-unguarded-order-submit`) and a unit test assert that every call site of `submit()` is inside a guard.

Arming in Live requires a deliberate second action and announces assertively (CMP-229 a11y contract); a single keystroke can never arm in Live.

## Test plan

- **Security**: covered by E30-X02 abuse cases (forged `arm_token`, replay after disarm, guard bypass via programmatic click).
- Coverage â‰¥80%.

## Security notes
Threats (STRIDE from E30-X01): **Spoofing** a forged or replayed `arm_token`; **Tampering** with the persisted confirmation policy to disable LIVE confirmation; **Elevation** by dispatching a submit programmatically outside the guard; clickjacking an armed one-click control. CMP-229 is an `aria-pressed` switch whose accessible name states scope and state ("One-click trading: locked"). Arm and auto-disarm changes are announced **assertively** (`role="alert"`), because a silent disarm is a safety problem. The environment band (SCR-075) is a `role="status"` landmark read early in document order, and every trading panel repeats the environment in its accessible name ("Order ticket â€” LIVE â€” Main"). The distinction is text + icon + pattern, never colour alone. On SCR-076 the confirm button's accessible name restates the whole order and `Enter` only confirms after 400 ms to prevent double-entry pass-through; for LIVE market orders the confirm button is never default-focused.

## Performance notes
Arm/disarm round trip â‰¤400 ms; local disarm on a kill-switch or disconnect event is immediate (<1 s from the WS event, no network dependency). SCR-076 opens within 100 ms from already-loaded state with no fetch, preserving the budget #4 clickâ†’ack allowance.

## Observability
Audit `order.arm_toggled` `{armed, scope, ttl, environment, reason?}`; `order.auto_disarmed{reason}`; `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled`. Analytics `order.confirmation_shown`, `order.confirmation_cancelled`. Metric `cv_ticket_arm_state_seconds{state}` and `cv_ticket_guard_blocked_total{reason}`.

title: Wire trading hotkeys with focus suppression and hold-to-confirm
body:
## Context
US-ORD-006 (Must): "hotkeys for buy/sell, size, flatten and cancel-all, so that execution keeps pace with my read." Hotkeys are where speed and safety collide: the same keystroke that makes a scalper viable can fire a market order into a text field typo. The story's own NFRs set the rules â€” **hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms client-side, destructive keys default to hold-to-confirm, everything remappable** â€” and SCR-113's audit rule adds that rebinding a *trading* action is itself an audited event.

This Story owns the trading hotkey **runtime** and the trading rows of the hotkey editor. The editor screen SCR-113 as a whole is a settings surface owned by the settings area; here we contribute its trading-action group, its caution treatment and its conflict rules for destructive bindings.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-006** (and the trading slice of US-SET-002). Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-113** (trading-action rows), **SCR-040** (arm display only).
- Bound actions: buy market, sell market, buy limit at bid, sell limit at ask, set size preset `1..4`, cycle sizing mode, toggle reduce-only, submit (`Ctrl+Enter`), clear ticket (`Esc`), arm/disarm (`Ctrl+Shift+T`), cancel-all on symbol, flatten. (Flatten/cancel-all *execution* belongs to E31/E29; this Story binds the keys and applies the confirm policy, dispatching through the shared intent layer.)
- Persistence in `hotkey_profiles` (`21-database-schema.md` Â§3.8.5) via `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys`, `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}` and `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}/activate`; `requires_arm` respected â€” a trading binding does nothing while locked, and says so.
- **Focus suppression**: trading hotkeys never fire while focus is in a text field, a `contenteditable`, or a modal that is not the confirmation modal; a subtle persistent indicator shows that they are suppressed (US-ORD-006 scenario 3).
- **Hold-to-confirm**: destructive actions (flatten, cancel-all, reverse) default to a hold gesture with a visible progress affordance and an announced countdown; the alternatives are immediate and dialog, chosen per action in SCR-114.
- Conflict rules on SCR-113's trading rows: single-letter bindings for destructive commands are refused while the "require a modifier for destructive commands" safety option is on; conflicts name the conflicting action.
- **CMP-022 Kbd**, **CMP-064 KeyboardShortcutRow**, **CMP-054 SearchBox**, **CMP-027 InlineError** on SCR-113; **CMP-229 ArmToggle** for the arm binding.

## Out of scope
The full SCR-113 editor (capture mode, import/export, non-trading actions) â€” settings area; flatten/cancel-all execution semantics (E31, US-ORD-010); chart/DOM-scoped keys (E31); OS-level global hotkeys in Electron (E44/shell).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Buy market (US-ORD-006)
  Given one-click is armed, demo environment, and B is mapped to buy market
  When I press B with the chart or ticket focused and no text field active
  Then a market buy for the active size is submitted to the active target with a native stop attached per the profile
  And the gesture-to-request time is under 50 ms
Scenario: Flatten applies the confirm policy (US-ORD-006)
  When I press the flatten key
  Then the configured policy applies (immediate, hold-to-confirm or dialog)
  And on confirmation the position closes and working orders are cancelled, reported as one operation
Scenario: Hotkey while unfocused (US-ORD-006)
  Given focus is inside a text field
  When I press B
  Then no order is submitted and a subtle indicator shows that trading hotkeys are suppressed
Scenario: Locked means inert (US-ORD-005 interaction)
  Given one-click is locked
  When I press a trading hotkey
  Then nothing is submitted and the reason "One-click trading is locked" is announced
Scenario: Destructive single-letter binding refused
  Given the "require a modifier for destructive commands" option is on
  When I try to bind flatten to F alone
  Then the binding is refused with a message naming the rule, and the previous binding is retained
Scenario: Rebinding a trading action is audited
  When I change the binding of any trading action
  Then hotkey.trading_binding_changed is written to the audit log with the before and after values
```

## Technical notes / design
A single keyboard dispatcher subscribes at the window level in the capture phase, resolves the active `hotkey_profiles` binding map (O(1) lookup), and checks, in this order: (1) focus target is not a text-entry context; (2) no blocking modal; (3) `requires_arm` satisfied; (4) environment and arm state resolved (the E30-S04 fail-closed guard); (5) confirm policy. Only then does it dispatch through the shared ticket intent layer. Ordering matters: the arm check must precede any side-effectful preview so a locked session cannot even warm the request.

To hit the 50 ms budget the dispatch path must not wait on React rendering â€” the handler calls `order-ticket-core.submit()` directly through the store (per the E30-K01/ADR placement) and lets the UI catch up.

Hold-to-confirm uses `pointerdown`/`keydown` with a configurable hold duration (default 600 ms), cancels on early release, and exposes the progress both visually and as an `aria-live` countdown announced at most once per 200 ms.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: dispatcher precedence order; suppression in input/textarea/contenteditable/select and inside modals; `requires_arm` gating; hold-to-confirm complete/cancel; conflict detection incl. the destructive-modifier rule; binding persistence and activation.
- **Perf**: a benchmark asserting keydownâ†’`submit()` call under 50 ms p95 on the loaded workspace (harness from E30-K01).
- **Integration**: profile activation switches the map without a reload; `requires_arm=false` on a non-trading action still works while locked.
- **E2E**: armed hotkey buy on demo; suppressed hotkey in a text field; hold-to-confirm flatten (E30-Q02).
- **axe**: SCR-113 trading rows; bindings readable as text.

## Security notes
Threats: a malicious or accidental key sequence firing an order (mitigated by arm + suppression + hold-to-confirm); a tampered local binding map firing an unintended action (mitigated because the *action semantics* come from the app, not from the stored map â€” only the key is stored â€” and every order is re-authorised and re-validated server-side); binding changes as a social-engineering vector (mitigated by the audit event). Data classification: user preference data, no secrets. Security label applies because this is an order-placement path (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8).

## Accessibility notes
Every hotkey has a visible, focusable UI equivalent â€” the keyboard is an accelerator, never the only path (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). Suppression state is exposed in text, not only as an icon. The hold-to-confirm progress is announced. SCR-113 capture mode has a keyboard-only alternative (choose modifiers and key from selects) and bindings are readable as text for screen-reader users. Announcements of refusal ("One-click trading is locked") are assertive, since the user expected an order to be placed.

## Performance notes
Hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms p95 client-side (US-ORD-006 NFR), measured under a loaded workspace. Binding lookup is O(1) against a precomputed map; the map is rebuilt only on profile change, never per keystroke.

## Observability
Audit `hotkey.trading_binding_changed` `{action, before, after}`; `orders.submit{source:"hotkey"}`. Analytics `hotkey.fired{action}`, `hotkey.suppressed{reason}`. Metric `cv_ticket_hotkey_dispatch_ms`.

title: Add the pre-trade risk preview and account / trade-group selector
body:
## Context
US-ORD-014 (Should): "a compact preview of what an order will do, so that I never submit blind." The roadmap adds the multi-account half: "account/trade-group selector with the fan-out preview".

The preview is not cosmetic. `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` runs the **full fan-out pipeline** (`24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 sizing, Â§9.4 fan-out) without submitting, returning exactly what each leg would send and, crucially, which legs would be **rejected** and why (cap breach, symbol not allowed, insufficient margin, rate budget exhausted). Showing that before the user commits is what turns a partial fan-out failure from a surprise into a decision.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-014**, plus the selector slice of **SCR-061**. Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-061** (selector + preview only), **SCR-076** (the fan-out variant of the confirmation, listing every leg).
- **CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel** extended to the full preview: resulting position size, average entry, initial margin, estimated liquidation price, risk in USDT and in R, and fees (from `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate`).
- **CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip** for the estimated slippage on market orders.
- **CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect** + trade-group selection: single account (SCR-060) or a named trade group (SCR-061); groups are read from `GET /api/v1/trade-groups` (CRUD is E28) with per-account enable/disable respected.
- Fan-out preview via `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, debounced (`CV_TICKET_PREVIEW_DEBOUNCE_MS`, default 80 ms), showing an aggregate that expands per account, with each would-be-rejected leg listed with its reason.
- **CMP-232 LimitsChip** showing the **binding** constraint by name and its authority (profile / exchange / global), fed by `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` and the instrument filters.
- Stale-input handling: when wallet/balance data is stale the preview shows what it can, marks the stale inputs, and disables risk-based sizing (US-ORD-014 scenario 3).

## Out of scope
Trade-group CRUD and per-account enable/disable editing (E28, SCR-062); fan-out execution, the rate-limit governor, partial-failure unwind (E34); the positions/orders blotter (E29); per-account PnL views (E34/E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview (US-ORD-014)
  Given a configured ticket on a single account
  Then the preview shows resulting position size, average entry, initial margin, estimated liquidation price, risk in USDT and in R, and fees
Scenario: Group preview (US-ORD-014)
  Given a trade group of three accounts is selected as the target
  Then the preview aggregates across accounts and can be expanded to show each account's own resolved quantity, stop and margin
Scenario: Rejected legs are shown before committing
  Given one account's profile disallows the symbol and another has insufficient margin
  Then both legs are listed as would-be-rejected with their reasons, the aggregate excludes them, and submitting is still possible for the remaining legs only after an explicit acknowledgement
Scenario: Preview unavailable (US-ORD-014)
  Given account balance data is stale and cannot be refreshed
  Then the preview shows what it can, marks the stale inputs explicitly, and risk-based sizing is disabled with a stated reason
Scenario: Preview never places an order
  When the preview endpoint is called on every keystroke
  Then no state is mutated, no idempotency key is consumed, and calls are debounced and rate-limited client-side
Scenario: Manager scope
  Given a manager who has been granted only two of the group's three accounts
  Then the selector offers only the granted accounts and the server refuses the ungranted one with 403 rather than silently narrowing the group
```

## Technical notes / design
`POST /trade-groups/preview` is documented as safe to call on every keystroke and is rate-limited rather than idempotency-keyed â€” but "safe" is not "free": the client debounces at 80 ms, cancels in-flight requests with `AbortController`, and renders the last-known preview greyed while a new one is in flight rather than blanking (a blanking preview during fast typing is worse than a slightly stale one, provided staleness is marked).

Liquidation price and margin are **estimates** and are labelled as such per architecture principle P10 ("estimated is labelled"), with the `(estimated)` chip.

The aggregate must never be silently partial: if any leg's data is unavailable, the aggregate states "aggregate excludes sub_002 (state unknown)" rather than presenting a smaller number as complete â€” the same rule `GET /risk/summary` applies server-side when it refuses a partial aggregate with `403 account_scope_denied`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: preview field rendering incl. estimated labelling; aggregate vs per-account expansion; rejected-leg listing per reason; stale marking and the risk-sizing disable; debounce and abort behaviour; partial-aggregate refusal copy.
- **Contract**: `CreateTradeGroupRequest` sent to `/trade-groups/preview` and `TradeGroupPreview` parsed, validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Integration**: fixtures for all four rejection reasons (cap breach, symbol not allowed, insufficient margin, rate budget exhausted); a 403 account-scope response.
- **Perf**: preview recompute path within 100 ms of an input change for the locally-derived parts (US-ORD-014 NFR), with the network part excluded and measured separately.
- **E2E**: three-account group preview then submit, in E30-Q02.
- **axe**: expansion control, table semantics of the per-leg breakdown.

## Security notes
Account scope is the central threat: the selector must be populated from the server's granted-accounts list only, and every preview and submit re-authorises server-side (`scope: granted_accounts`). A manager must not be able to discover the existence of ungranted accounts through the group selector â€” groups containing ungranted accounts are shown with those legs omitted **and** labelled as narrowed, so no hidden fan-out occurs. Preview responses contain financial data and are account-scoped; they are never cached across account switches. Covered by the E30-X02 abuse-case suite.

## Accessibility notes
The per-account breakdown is a real `<table>` with row headers per account, not a div grid, so screen-reader users can navigate it. The binding limit is named in text and announced when it changes ("Blocked by daily loss cap: 480 of 500 USDT used"). Every estimate carries the word "estimated" in its accessible name, not only a visual chip. The expand/collapse control states the number of legs. Stale inputs are marked in text.

## Performance notes
Local preview recompute â‰¤100 ms (US-ORD-014 NFR); the debounce must not push the perceived update beyond 200 ms. The preview must not contribute to the budget #4 submit path â€” it runs on a separate connection concern and is cancelled on submit.

## Observability
Analytics `ticket.preview_expanded`, `ticket.preview_leg_rejected{reason}`, `ticket.group_selected{legCount}`. Metric `cv_ticket_preview_latency_ms`. No audit event (preview mutates nothing), but a submit following a preview records the preview's correlation id so the journal can show what the user was shown.

## Context
US-ORD-012 (Should): "saved combinations of order, bracket and size, so that repeated setups are one click." Templates are the user-facing half; **SCR-114 Trading defaults** is the settings half that decides what a *fresh* ticket looks like and, importantly, which confirmation policy applies. SCR-114 also carries a hard product rule: **user defaults can never exceed the per-account profile limits set by the owner**, and each limit is shown inline as a ceiling.

- Template model: name, order type, side, sizing spec, bracket spec, TIF and flags, optional pinned account or trade group. Stored per user through `GET|PUT /api/v1/settings` (templates live in the user-settings document; a dedicated migration is added only if the settings document exceeds its size guard â€” recorded as a decision on the ticket).
- Template list with apply, rename, delete, duplicate and **bind to a hotkey** (through the E30-S05 dispatcher and `hotkey_profiles`).
- Applying a template populates every field and applies the pinned target if the template has one; a template pinning an account the user cannot trade is shown **disabled with the reason**, never silently applied to a different account.
- SCR-114 sections: default order type, TIF, default qty and the preset ladder, default sizing rule (`fixed_qty` / `fixed_notional` / `pct_equity` / `risk_based`), default SL/TP offsets (ticks / % / R), confirm-before-send rules (always / live only / never when armed), one-click arm persistence, auto-reset ticket after send, sound on fill â€” with **separate DEMO and LIVE default sets**.
- Enforced rules on SCR-114: "skip confirmation" is unavailable for LIVE market orders; the default SL is mandatory and cannot be set to "none"; every limit is shown inline as a ceiling with a pointer to SCR-131 for per-account overrides.
- **CMP-040 FormField**, **CMP-065 FormSection**, **CMP-086 SettingsLayout**, **CMP-119 BracketEditor**, **CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons**, **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice**, **CMP-231 TifSelect**.

## Out of scope
Per-account profile editing (E28, SCR-131); algo/bracket templates that include emulated algos (E33); sharing or exporting templates between users (not in scope for v1); the hotkey editor screen itself (E30-S05 contributes its trading rows).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Template invalid for context (US-ORD-012)

Scenario: Defaults cannot exceed profile limits
  Given the account profile caps leverage at 10x
  When I set a default above that

Scenario: LIVE confirmation cannot be switched off for market orders
  Given the LIVE default set
  Then the "never confirm" option for market orders is disabled with a stated reason
  And attempting it via a crafted settings request is refused server-side and audited
Scenario: The default stop cannot be "none"
  When I try to clear the default SL offset
  Then it is refused with the safety-invariant message and the SafetyInvariantNotice stays visible
Scenario: Templates contain no secrets
  Then an exported or stored template contains no API key, token or account credential of any kind
```

## Technical notes / design
Templates are validated against the current context at **render** time, not only at apply time, so a disabled template explains itself before the user reaches for it. Validation reuses `order-ticket-core.validate()` against a synthetic draft, so template validity and ticket validity can never disagree.

DEMO and LIVE default sets are stored as two distinct documents keyed by environment; switching environments switches the applied set and never carries a LIVE-unsafe setting (like skipped confirmation) across from DEMO. Defaults apply to **newly opened tickets only**; existing tickets keep their state (SCR-114 performance note). Save round-trip â‰¤400 ms.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: template save/apply/rename/delete/duplicate; disabled-template conditions (ungranted account, disallowed symbol, unavailable order type); defaults-vs-profile ceiling enforcement per field; LIVE confirmation exclusion; mandatory default SL; DEMO/LIVE set isolation.
- **Contract**: settings payload validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/settings`.
- **Integration**: a settings write that violates a profile ceiling is refused server-side (not only client-side).
- **Security test**: serialised templates are asserted to contain no secret-shaped values.
- **axe + visual** on all SCR-114 sections and the template list.

## Security notes
Threats: tampering with stored defaults to disable LIVE confirmation (mitigated â€” the rule is enforced server-side and the attempt is audited at high severity as `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled`); a template pinning an ungranted account as a scope-probing oracle (mitigated â€” the disabled reason must not reveal the existence or name of an account the user cannot see; it says "this template targets an account you cannot trade"); secrets in templates (mitigated â€” a test asserts the shape). Every defaults change is audited as `trading_defaults.changed {key, before, after, environment}`.

## Accessibility notes
Fieldsets per topic; every numeric field states its unit; the confirmation-policy radio group states the **consequence** of each option, not just its name. Disabled templates and disabled options always state why in text. The ceiling annotations are associated with their field via `aria-describedby`, so a screen-reader user hears the cap when they enter the field rather than only on failure.

## Performance notes
Save round-trip â‰¤400 ms (SCR-114). Template apply populates the ticket within the 8 ms recompute budget. The template list is rendered from already-loaded settings â€” no fetch on open.

## Observability
Audit `trading_defaults.changed`, `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled` (high severity). Analytics `template.saved`, `template.applied{hasPinnedTarget}`, `template.disabled_shown{reason}`.

- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; Storybook for the template list and every SCR-114 section incl. the refusal states.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on the ceiling annotations and consequence copy.
