title: Build the SCR-077 rejection drawer and the SCR-158 rate-limited ticket state
body:
## Context
Every rejection the user cannot understand is a trade they will re-attempt blindly. SCR-077 exists so that "why did my order do that" has exactly one answer surface: the exchange's verbatim `retCode`/`retMsg`, a plain-language translation, what CandleViewer actually sent (redacted), and a retry-with-corrections path. SCR-158 covers the specific case where nothing was sent at all because the per-UID rate budget was exhausted (Bybit code `10018`).

Both are consumed by the ticket but are separately testable presentation surfaces, which is why they are a Task rather than folded into E30-S01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screens **SCR-077** (order rejection detail drawer), **SCR-158** (rate-limited state). Components **CMP-046 Drawer**, **CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock**, **CMP-021 Link**, **CMP-023 Progress Bar**, **CMP-028 Callout/Banner**, **CMP-035 Countdown**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**.
- Data: `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` (`OrderDiagnostics` â€” ordered `order_events` chain plus redacted exchange request/response pairs and the reconciliation verdict), lazily fetched only when the user expands the raw payload.
- Written plain-language copy for each common rejection: insufficient margin, reduce-only violation, tick/lot rounding, leverage limit, risk-limit tier, rate limit, position-mode mismatch, post-only would-cross, `native_stop_required`, `trading_disabled` (kill-switch), account scope denied.
- "Retry with corrections" that pre-fills a corrected ticket **only where the fix is unambiguous** (tick/lot rounding, reduce-only off, reprice off the spread) â€” never for margin or risk-cap rejections, where the correct action is a human decision.
- SCR-158: per-scope variants (exchange per-UID, backend per-user, fan-out budget), the retry-after countdown as absolute and relative time, which actions are **held** versus dropped, which accounts were served in a fan-out, and a link to SCR-147.
- Held-action queue: user actions refused for rate-limit reasons are held, not dropped, and are replayed only after an explicit confirmation â€” never silently.

## Out of scope
The rate-limit governor itself (E34); the audit-log browser linked from the drawer (E42); backend diagnostics assembly (E29); SCR-147 (admin rate-limit screen, E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A rejection is explained, not just reported
  Given the exchange rejects an order with retCode 110007
  When the rejection drawer opens
  Then the verbatim exchange message is shown as quoted text with a plain-language translation beneath it
  And the correlation id is selectable and the raw payload is available on explicit expansion only
Scenario: Retry with corrections only where unambiguous
  Given a tick-size rounding rejection
  Then a "retry with corrections" action pre-fills a corrected ticket and the correction is stated
  And for an insufficient-margin rejection no auto-correction is offered
Scenario: Nothing secret is ever rendered
  Given the raw payload is expanded
  Then no API key, signature, token or KEK-derived value appears, and the redaction is asserted by test
Scenario: Rate-limited state holds rather than drops
  Given the per-UID budget is exhausted for an account
  Then SCR-158 names the throttled scope, the retry-after time as absolute and relative values, and what is still permitted
  And queued actions are held and replayed only after explicit confirmation
Scenario: Fan-out partial rate-limiting names the accounts
  Given three of five accounts were served and two were starved
  Then the banner names which accounts were served and which were not, and links to the group's reconciliation state
```

## Technical notes / design
Drawer opens from already-received rejection data â€” no fetch in the common case (SCR-077 performance note); `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` is fetched lazily on expansion and is **audited on read**, so the fetch must not be speculative or prefetched.

Error copy is co-located with the code map in `order-ticket-core/errors.ts` so the inline message, the drawer translation and the toast can never diverge. An exhaustiveness test fails when a new backend error code has no copy.

Countdown announcements are throttled to at most one per 10 s (SCR-158 a11y note) while the visual countdown ticks every second.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥85% on the copy/mapping module, â‰¥80% on the components)**: one case per documented rejection reason asserting code â†’ translation â†’ correction availability; redaction assertion against a payload seeded with key-shaped and signature-shaped strings; held-queue replay requiring confirmation; countdown throttling.
- **Contract**: `OrderDiagnostics` parsed per `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Integration**: a `429` response drives SCR-158; a `502` exchange error drives SCR-077.
- **axe**: `role="alert"` on drawer open, `role="status"` on the rate-limit banner, quoted-text semantics.

## Security notes
The diagnostics endpoint is the **only** place raw exchange retCode/retMsg and request/response pairs are exposed, it is redacted server-side, and reading it is audited. The client must not log the payload to the console or to any client-side telemetry sink. A test seeds credential-shaped strings into a fixture payload and asserts none reach the DOM or any analytics call.

## Accessibility notes
The drawer announces itself with `role="alert"` on open. The verbatim exchange message is marked up as quoted text with the plain-language translation as adjacent prose, so a screen reader distinguishes the two voices. The correlation id and the raw payload are selectable text, not images. body:
## Context
The order ticket is the only screen in CandleViewer where a wrong pixel costs money. Before we draw it we need evidence about three things the screens catalogue currently asserts rather than proves: (1) what a trader actually looks at in the two seconds before submitting; (2) how they expect an *armed* state to feel different from a locked one; (3) what they do when an order is rejected â€” re-read, retry, or abandon.

This research also has to test a decision that is already locked and cannot be changed by the findings: the **mandatory native stop-loss** and the **arm/lock + environment badge** requirement. ## Scope / Deliverables

- Two concept probes: (a) arm/lock treatments â€” persistent badge vs. banner vs. tinted chrome; (b) sizing-mode switching â€” segmented control vs. mode-per-field.
- A timed task: "size this trade to risk 0.5% with a stop under that swing low, then place it" â€” measured to establish the baseline the 8 ms/50 ms budgets serve.
- Deliverable: a findings report in `docs/plan/` research notes format with prioritised implications, a quote bank, and an explicit list of questions the research could **not** answer (to be resolved by design QA or by the E30-Q06 exploratory charter).


Sessions run against a clickable stimulus, not the live app, so participants cannot place real orders. Consent covers recording and internal use only. Participants are told the product is self-hosted and single-owner so they do not reason about multi-tenant concerns that do not exist here.

At least one participant uses the product with keyboard-only navigation, and the discussion guide includes a keyboard-only pass of the placement task, so the a11y requirements in `05-accessibility-standard.md` are informed by a real user rather than only by audit.

The timed sizing task establishes the human baseline the `8 ms` recompute and `50 ms` hotkey budgets are meant to protect; the report states the observed human times so engineering knows what headroom actually matters.

## Context

If they ship as one-off compositions inside the order-ticket feature they will be re-invented by E31 (chart/DOM trading), E33 (algo builders) and E36/E37 (rule editors), and the safety treatments â€” armed, live, unprotected, estimated â€” will drift between surfaces. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.1 makes this a DoR condition: "any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off."

Motion matters here for a specific safety reason: the difference between "submitting" and "submitted" must be perceptible without being decorative, and the armed state must read as a sustained condition rather than a transient flash.

## Scope / Deliverables

Every motion has a `prefers-reduced-motion` alternative that conveys the same state change without movement.

Numeric values use tabular monospace figures everywhere so that a changing price does not shift layout â€” a shifting layout under a cursor is how a wrong price gets clicked. Specs must avoid effects that force layout on every tick (no box-shadow animation on price change, no per-tick reflow); the value-change highlight is specified as a compositor-only property.

`03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, executed and signed off by QA before a Story can reach Done. For an order ticket that plan is also the safety net for the things unit tests structurally cannot see: that a *human* cannot get an order out without a stop, cannot mistake demo for live, and cannot fire while locked.

Writing the plan first (S16, alongside the first Stories) also forces the fixtures to exist before the E2E work in E30-Q02 needs them.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Per-screen exploratory-charter seeds for SCR-060, SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-114, SCR-158.
- **Fixtures**: recorded Bybit demo responses for accepted, partially filled, rejected (post-only would cross `110007`, insufficient margin, reduce-only violation, tick/lot violation, leverage limit, risk-limit tier, position-mode mismatch), `10018` rate-limited, `502` exchange error, and a `422 native_stop_required`. Instrument fixtures for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and 1000PEPEUSDT covering distinct tick/lot/min-notional shapes. Profile fixtures covering each sizing mode, a leverage cap, a symbol allowlist, a daily-loss cap near its limit and an account with the native-SL invariant opted out.
- A **risk-based test matrix** ranking scenarios by consequence: anything that could result in an unintended, unprotected or wrongly-sized order is P0 and is executed every regression cycle, not sampled.
- Entry/exit criteria for the E30 test cycle and the definition of a blocking defect for this Epic.

## Out of scope
Automation (E30-Q02), perf scripts (E30-Q03), chaos (E30-Q04), a11y audit (E30-Q05), backend OMS testing (E29's own QA tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Then each Gherkin scenario in US-ORD-001..006 and US-ORD-013 maps to at least one test-plan step with an observable expected result
Scenario: Fixtures exist for every failure the UI claims to handle
  Then each rejection reason with written copy in the E30-D06 copy deck has a corresponding recorded fixture
Scenario: Safety scenarios are P0 and unsampled
  Then every scenario that could produce an unintended, unprotected or mis-sized order is marked P0 and included in every regression cycle
Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer unfamiliar with the Epic
  Then they can execute any step from the plan alone without asking a clarifying question
```

## Technical notes / design
Fixtures are recorded from the real Bybit **demo** environment and stored in `packages/fixtures/bybit/` (the `orders/` set), in a capture's dated directory, each file with its `manifest.json` entry naming the capture date and the endpoint (`packages/fixtures/bybit/README.md`), so they can be re-captured when Bybit changes a response shape (risk R6 Feed rot). Each fixture carries the exact `retCode`/`retMsg` â€” invented error payloads would make the copy deck untestable.

The plan distinguishes **client-blocked** from **server-rejected** for every validation: they are different code paths with different user-visible behaviour, and conflating them in the plan would let a client-side-only guard pass as if it were enforcement.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test plan. Its own quality gate: reviewed by the E30 engineering lead and the Security engineer (for the safety and abuse scenarios) before it is used.

## Security notes
Fixtures must be scrubbed of account ids, balances, keys and signatures before being committed; a secret-scanning check runs over the fixture directory. The plan includes the negative security scenarios that QA (not Security) can execute black-box: submitting while locked, submitting with a manipulated account selection, disabling LIVE confirmation.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes a keyboard-only execution of the core placement path as a standard step in every cycle, so a11y regression is caught by routine QA and not only by the dedicated audit in E30-Q05.

## Performance notes
The plan includes the observable side of the budgets: acknowledgement visible within 500 ms, preview updating within a perceptible 200 ms, no visible lag when typing into the price field on a loaded workspace. Instrumented measurement is E30-Q03's job.

Each P0 scenario names the audit event that must be present afterwards (`orders.submit`, `order.rejected`, `order.arm_toggled`), so QA verifies the audit trail as part of the functional pass rather than trusting it.

## Context
R3's E2E gate requires "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, fan-out, rule creation in both editors, alert firing, journal capture" (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4). This ticket delivers the **ticket** slice of that suite, running against the **demo** environment â€” never live, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `tests/e2e/order-ticket/` running in both the browser and the Electron shell:
  - `place-limit.spec` â€” keyboard-only limit order placement end to end, asserting the acknowledgement and the WS-driven state transition.
  - `place-market-armed.spec` â€” arm â†’ one-click market with the profile stop attached.
  - `hotkey.spec` â€” armed hotkey buy; hotkey suppressed in a text field; hotkey inert while locked.
  - `validation.spec` â€” client-blocked cases (min qty, tick, reduce-only without a position, missing native SL) asserting no network call is made.
  - `rejection.spec` â€” a seeded exchange rejection producing the inline error and the SCR-077 drawer with the verbatim message and the retained inputs.
  - `ratelimit.spec` â€” a seeded `10018` producing SCR-158 with a held action and an explicit replay confirmation.
  - `confirmation.spec` â€” demo skip-when-armed; live-shaped fixture refusing to skip for a market order; auto-cancel on inactivity.
  - `group-preview.spec` â€” three-account group preview with one would-be-rejected leg, then submit of the remaining legs after acknowledgement.
  - `templates.spec` â€” save, apply, and a disabled template with its reason.
- Deterministic test data: a dedicated demo account set and a fixture-seeded backend mode for the failure cases, so rejections do not depend on market conditions.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on every PR touching `apps/web/src/features/order-ticket` or `packages/order-ticket-core`, and nightly in full; flake budget â‰¤1%, with a quarantine process rather than a retry-until-green default.
- Trace/video artefacts retained for failures.

## Out of scope
Chart/DOM trading E2E (E31-Q02), fan-out execution E2E (E34), backend unit/integration tests (E29), perf measurement (E30-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite proves an order can be placed with the keyboard alone
  When place-limit.spec runs
  Then the entire path from focus entry to acknowledgement uses keyboard input only and passes in both browser and Electron
Scenario: Client-blocked cases prove no network call
  When validation.spec runs
  Then the network log shows zero requests to /api/v1/orders for each blocked case
Scenario: The suite never touches live
  Then every spec asserts the environment is demo before acting, and fails immediately if it is not
Scenario: Flake is controlled
  Given ten consecutive nightly runs
  Then the flake rate is at or below 1% and any flaky spec is quarantined with a tracking ticket rather than retried blindly
```

## Technical notes / design
Selectors are role- and name-based (`getByRole('button', {name: /submit buy/i})`), which doubles as a continuous check that the accessible names specified in E30-D05 are actually present â€” a broken accessible name breaks the E2E suite, which is exactly the coupling we want.

WS-driven assertions wait on the rendered state transition, never on a fixed timeout; the ack-timeout path is tested by holding the WS event back deliberately.

The live-policy test uses a **live-shaped fixture environment**, not a real live account: the environment flag is set to live in a sandboxed backend so the UI's live behaviour is exercised without any possibility of a real order.

## Test plan
Meta-tests: each spec is verified to fail when its feature is deliberately broken (mutation check on a sample of three specs), so a spec that passes vacuously is caught.

## Security notes
Test credentials are demo-only, injected from CI secrets, never committed, and scoped to accounts with no withdrawal permission (which the platform guarantees anyway). Traces and videos are scanned before retention because they can capture balances; artefacts are retained privately and expire after 14 days.

## Accessibility notes
Role/name-based selectors enforce the accessible-name contract. `keyboard-only.spec` behaviour is embedded in `place-limit.spec` rather than being a separate optional test, so it cannot be skipped when the suite is trimmed.

The suite asserts the *observable* budget (acknowledgement rendered within 500 ms on demo) but does not attempt statistical measurement â€” that is E30-Q03. Suite wall-clock â‰¤8 minutes so it can gate PRs.

Failing runs attach the correlation id of the last order request so a failure can be traced into backend logs without re-running.

title: Build the performance and load scripts for the ticket's latency budgets
body:
## Context
Three client budgets and one end-to-end budget govern this Epic, and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` treats budget #4 (order submit â†’ ack, p95 <300 ms demo) as a **hard gate**. E30-K01 measured them on a prototype; this ticket turns that into a repeatable, CI-runnable measurement that fails when a regression lands, rather than when someone notices the app feels slow.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark harness (promoted from E30-K01) measuring, on the reference loaded workspace (chart + footprint + DOM ladder live on demo data):
  - ticket recompute after price, qty and sizing-mode changes â€” budget **8 ms** (SCR-060);
  - gesture â†’ request dispatch for click, `Ctrl+Enter` and hotkey â€” the client share of budget #4, target **â‰¤20 ms**, and the **50 ms** hotkey budget (US-ORD-006);
  - preview local recompute â€” **100 ms** (US-ORD-014);
  - end-to-end click â†’ acknowledgement rendered against a demo account â€” budget #4, **p95 <300 ms**.
- A k6 script driving sustained ticket-shaped order flow against the demo backend at the per-UID limit for one hour, asserting zero lost acknowledgements and correct `10018` back-off (the R3 Load gate), with the ticket's own client behaviour observed under that pressure.
- CI wiring: the client benchmarks run nightly with a **+20% regression gate** against a stored baseline; the end-to-end budget is measured in the nightly demo run and reported, gating the R3 PRR rather than every PR (because it includes uncontrolled Bybit RTT).
- A results dashboard panel and the recorded figures fed into E30-T03's docs reconciliation.

## Out of scope
Backend-internal latency budgeting (E29/E34 own the â‰¤50 ms backend-added share), chart-engine FPS (E11/E46), fan-out load beyond the ticket's role in it (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every budget has an automated measurement
  Then recompute, dispatch, hotkey, preview and click-to-ack each have a scripted measurement reporting p50, p95 and p99
Scenario: A regression fails the build
  Given a deliberate 30% slowdown injected into the recompute path
  Then the nightly benchmark fails against the stored baseline
Scenario: Measurement is honest about what it includes
  Then each reported figure states whether it includes network and Bybit RTT, per the exclusion rules in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md section 2
Scenario: The suite runs under realistic contention
  Then measurements are taken with the chart engine and ladder actively rendering, not on an idle page
```

## Technical notes / design
Baselines are stored per hardware class; CI runners and the developer workstation are different classes and are never compared to each other. Each run records the build sha, the workspace definition and the WS traffic rate so a regression can be attributed rather than merely detected.

p95 is computed over â‰¥1 000 samples per metric; runs with a coefficient of variation above a threshold are rejected as noisy and repeated, rather than reported.

## Test plan
The harness self-tests: an injected artificial delay of a known size must be detected within 10% by each metric, proving the measurement is actually measuring the intended span.

## Security notes
Load scripts run against demo only and use demo credentials from CI secrets. The k6 script must respect the per-UID budget deliberately â€” a load test that ignores rate limits would both invalidate its own results and risk the demo account's standing.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (measurement tooling). Note that the announcement throttles specified in E30-D05 are part of what keeps the accessibility tree cheap; the harness records accessibility-tree recomputation cost as a secondary metric so a regression there is visible.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the performance work. Budgets: 8 ms recompute (SCR-060), â‰¤20 ms client dispatch and p95 <300 ms end to end (budget #4, Â§5.2), 50 ms hotkey (US-ORD-006), 100 ms preview (US-ORD-014), plus the one-hour sustained-flow Load gate.

## Observability
Publishes `cv_ticket_recompute_ms`, `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms`, `cv_ticket_hotkey_dispatch_ms` and `cv_ticket_preview_latency_ms` to the Grafana dashboard so the budgets are observable in staging continuously, not only during the benchmark window.

- [ ] Nightly CI wiring with the +20% regression gate; injected-slowdown test proves the gate works.

body:
## Context
R3's Chaos gate requires that "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out â€” all resume to a correct, reconciled state" (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4). The ticket's share of that is the **client's** behaviour when the ground moves under an order it has already sent: it must never invent a fill, never lose the user's inputs, never stay armed when it cannot verify that it should be, and never show a position as protected when the stop has not been confirmed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scripted fault injection against the demo stack, each asserting an observable UI outcome:
  1. **WS drop between ack and fill** â€” the ticket shows "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" after `CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`, and reconciles correctly on reconnect without duplicating the order.
  2. **REST timeout with the order actually placed** â€” the retry uses the same idempotency key and the server replays rather than double-placing; the UI ends in one order, not two.
  3. **Backend restart mid-submit** â€” the client surfaces a clear unknown state and reconciles from `GET /api/v1/orders` on recovery.
  4. **Kill-switch engaged while armed** â€” the client disarms within one second and a subsequent one-click submit is refused with `trading_disabled`.
  5. **Risk-cap lockout mid-ticket** â€” the submit affordance becomes blocked-by-lockout with the reason and the reset path stated.
  6. **Arm token expiry mid-gesture** â€” the submit is refused with `403`, the client reconciles to locked, and the user's inputs are retained.
  7. **Stop attach failure** â€” the entry is accepted but no exchange-side stop is confirmed; the ticket shows "order live, protective stop pending" and surfaces the critical alert, and never shows a plain "filled".
  8. **Stale wallet / `wallet` topic silence** â€” equity-derived sizing modes disable themselves rather than sizing from stale data.
  9. **Clock skew** between client and server â€” arm expiry is driven by the server's absolute `expires_at`, not by a local countdown drifting into an over-long armed window.
  10. **Rate-limit exhaustion mid-fan-out** â€” SCR-158 names served and unserved accounts and holds rather than drops the remaining intent.
- Each scenario scripted and repeatable in CI (nightly, not per-PR), with pass criteria stated as UI-observable outcomes.

## Out of scope
Backend recovery correctness itself (E29/E45 own reconciliation and failover), Postgres failover mechanics (E45), fan-out unwind semantics (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No invented outcomes
  Given any injected fault between submit and fill
  Then the UI never displays a filled or rejected state it has not observed on the orders or executions topic
Scenario: No duplicate orders
  Given a REST timeout on an order that actually reached the exchange
  When the user retries without changing any field
  Then exactly one order exists at the exchange and the UI shows exactly one
Scenario: Arming fails closed under every fault
  Given a kill-switch, a lockout, a token expiry or a disconnect
  Then the client ends in the locked state with the reason displayed, in every case
Scenario: A pending stop is never presented as protection
  Given the entry is filled and the stop is not confirmed
  Then the UI shows the pending-stop state in text and icon until the stop is observed
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection uses a proxy layer in front of the backend for network faults (drop, delay, kill), plus backend test hooks for kill-switch, lockout and stop-attach failure. Each scenario runs from a clean, known account state and asserts the final exchange-side truth via `GET /v5/order/realtime` through the backend, not only the UI â€” a UI that agrees with itself while disagreeing with the exchange is the exact failure we are hunting.

## Test plan
This ticket is the chaos test plan. Each scenario is also verified to *fail* when the corresponding guard is disabled, proving it discriminates.

## Security notes
Chaos runs on demo with demo credentials only. Scenario 4 (kill-switch) and scenario 5 (lockout) double as security assertions â€” the client must not be able to proceed by ignoring either, and the server refusal is verified independently of the UI.

## Accessibility notes
Each degraded state's announcement is asserted, not just its rendering: reconciling, pending-stop, locked-by-kill-switch and rate-limited must all be announced (the first three assertively), since a screen-reader user otherwise has no way to learn that the world changed under them.

## Performance notes
The reconciling threshold (`CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`, 2 000 ms) is validated here: too short and normal demo latency produces false reconciling states; too long and the user is left believing an unconfirmed order is fine.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected audit and metric side effects (`order.blocked_ratelimited`, `order.auto_disarmed{reason}`, the naked-position critical alert), so a silent failure of instrumentation is itself caught.

- [ ] All ten scenarios scripted, runnable nightly, and passing.

body:
## Context

E30-D05 specified the a11y contract at design time; this ticket verifies the built product against it, with a real screen reader, not only with axe.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Keyboard-only pass** of the full numbered sequence from E30-D05, including escaping every state, the confirmation modal's focus trap and focus return, and the `Enter`-after-400 ms rule.
- **Contrast verification** in the built product for every state including disabled, armed, live and pending-stop, in both themes.
- **Reduced-motion verification**: every motion-specified state change still conveys its change with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **Announcement-rate verification**: live regions respect the specified throttles under a live `ticker` feed â€” over-announcing is filed as a defect, not tolerated.
- Findings filed as Bugs with severity; all serious/critical fixed before the Epic closes; a written audit report attached.

## Out of scope
Chart/DOM trading a11y (E31-Q05), rule-editor a11y (E36/E37), the chart's DOM-mirror (E11), design-side review (E30-D05).

## Scope / Deliverables

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§2.1 makes a STRIDE kickoff mandatory for any Epic touching the OMS or order placement, and `30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4 requires all Critical/High findings closed before the R3 train can close. The order ticket is the **human-facing entry point to money movement**: it is where an attacker (or an accident) would try to get an unintended, unprotected, or wrongly-scoped order out.

This model must be produced **before** E30-S04 (arm/lock, environment, confirmation) is built, because S04's design is precisely the mitigation set â€” building it first and modelling afterwards would make the model a rationalisation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model for the ticket's trust boundaries: browser/Electron renderer â†” backend API, renderer â†” local storage (settings, templates, hotkeys, arm state), user â†” UI (the human factors boundary, which is where arm/lock and the environment badge live).
- Per-category enumeration with at least the following, each rated and mitigated:
  - **Spoofing**: forged or replayed `arm_token`; a session replay placing an order; a spoofed environment value making live look like demo.
  - **Tampering**: local settings tampered to disable LIVE confirmation; a tampered hotkey map; a tampered template pinning another account; an altered preset ladder exceeding profile caps; request tampering between the client's preview and its submit.
  - **Repudiation**: an order placed with no attributable audit trail; a binding change or defaults change not audited; a rejection viewed without an audit entry.
  - **Information disclosure**: account existence leaked through the group/template selector to a manager without scope; balances or exposure leaked in a preview across an account switch; credentials or signatures rendered in the rejection drawer or logged client-side.
  - **Denial of service**: preview called on every keystroke exhausting the per-UID budget and starving real orders; a held-action queue growing unbounded; an unthrottled live region.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a submit dispatched outside `CMP-139`; a manager submitting to an ungranted account; the invariant opt-out reachable from the ticket; skipping the confirmation policy on LIVE.
- A data-flow diagram of the ticket's order path annotated with the trust boundaries, reusing `20-architecture.md` Â§10.2 as the backend half.
- For each threat: the existing control, the gap (if any), the owning ticket, and a residual-risk rating. Gaps become concrete requirements on E30-S04/S06/S07 or on E30-X02's abuse-case suite â€” a threat with no owning ticket is not an acceptable outcome.
- Alignment with `04-security-program.md` controls and the R3 Security gate.

## Out of scope
Backend OMS threat modelling (E29-X01), key vault (E27-X01), fan-out and rate-limit abuse (E34), RBAC matrix implementation (E09/E27-X03), pen-testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is populated with concrete, product-specific threats

Scenario: Every threat has a control and an owner
  Then each threat names its mitigating control and the ticket that implements or verifies it, or is explicitly accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off
Scenario: The model gates the design it protects
  Then the model is complete and reviewed before E30-S04 starts implementation
Scenario: Critical and High findings are tracked to closure
  Then each Critical/High threat is linked to a verification in E30-X02 or E30-X03 and closed before the R3 train gate
```

## Technical notes / design
The human-factors boundary is modelled explicitly and is unusual enough to state: the user *is* an attack surface here, because a hurried trader who misreads demo as live has been "successfully attacked" by the UI. Threats in that category are mitigated by design constraints (always-visible environment, arm off by default, no default-focused confirm on LIVE market) rather than by code alone, and they are verified by E30-Q05's and E30-D07's passes.

The model records that **client-side controls are defence in depth only**: every client check has a named server-side counterpart, and any client check *without* one is itself a finding.

## Test plan
The model's outputs are tested, not the model itself: each Critical/High threat maps to an abuse-case test in E30-X02 or a scenario in E30-Q04, and the model is reviewed at E30-X03 to confirm every mapping was executed.

This ticket is the security work. Standard: `04-security-program.md`; STRIDE per Epic per `00-planning-brief.md`. Data classification for this surface: financial, account-scoped; no secrets are handled by the ticket itself, which is a deliberate property to preserve.

title: Implement the abuse-case suite, scope assertions and SAST rules for the ticket
body:
## Context
A threat model that is not executed is an opinion. This ticket turns E30-X01's Critical and High threats into **automated tests and static rules** that run in CI, so that the guarantees hold not only on the day of the review but on every subsequent commit â€” including commits made by other Epics that touch the same surfaces (E31, E33, E34 all reuse this ticket's intent layer).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case test suite** (`tests/security/order-ticket/`), each derived from a named threat:
  - forged `arm_token`, expired `arm_token`, and an `arm_token` replayed after disarm â†’ all refused server-side with `403`, audited, no order created;
  - a one-click order submitted with **no** `arm_token` â†’ refused;
  - a submit dispatched programmatically outside `CMP-139` â†’ impossible by construction (lint) and refused at runtime (assertion test);
  - a crafted `PlaceOrderRequest` omitting `stop_loss` on an invariant-required account â†’ `422 native_stop_required`, audited;
  - a crafted request with a stop on the wrong side of entry â†’ refused;
  - a manager submitting to an ungranted `exchange_account_id` â†’ `403`, no state change, audit row present;
  - a manager previewing a trade group containing an ungranted account â†’ the ungranted leg omitted **and** labelled, never silently included;
  - a settings write disabling LIVE market confirmation â†’ refused server-side and audited at high severity;
  - a tampered hotkey map binding a destructive action to a bare letter with the safety option on â†’ refused;
  - idempotency-key collision attempted across sessions â†’ rejected, no cross-session replay;
  - `10018` storm induced via preview spam â†’ client-side rate limiting holds, real orders are not starved.
- **RBAC/scope assertion matrix** for every ticket-originated route Ã— role (owner, manager with grant, manager without grant, viewer), asserting `403` + no state change + an audit row for every disallowed combination â€” the ticket's contribution to R3 exit criterion 10.
- **SAST rules**: a Semgrep rule set banning (a) `submit()` call sites outside the guard wrapper, (b) rendering of any field named like a credential/signature in the diagnostics view, (c) `console.log` of an order payload or diagnostics response, (d) persistence of the arm token to any storage API. Wired as a blocking CI check.
- **DAST**: an OWASP ZAP pass over the trading routes checking CSP (`frame-ancestors 'none'` for clickjacking of the armed control), security headers, and that no order endpoint is reachable without authentication.
- **Secrets check** extended over test fixtures and Playwright artefacts.

## Out of scope
Backend OMS abuse cases (E29-X02), key vault (E27), fan-out rate governor abuse (E34), the full RBAC matrix across all routes (E09/E42 own the global matrix â€” this contributes the ticket's rows), pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Critical and High threat has an executable test
  Then each Critical/High threat from E30-X01 maps to at least one test in this suite, and the mapping table is complete
Scenario: The suite fails when a control is removed
  Given the arm-token server-side check is disabled in a mutation build
  Then the corresponding abuse-case test fails
Scenario: Scope violations produce 403, no state change and an audit row
  Given every role and every ticket-originated route
  Then each disallowed combination returns 403, mutates nothing, and writes an audit entry
Scenario: SAST rules block, not warn
  Given a commit introducing a submit call outside the guard wrapper
  Then CI fails on the Semgrep rule and the commit cannot merge
```

## Technical notes / design
Abuse cases are executed against the **backend**, using crafted requests rather than the UI, because the point is to prove the server does not rely on the client. Where a control is genuinely client-only (the hold-to-confirm gesture, focus suppression), the test says so explicitly and the threat model records the residual risk â€” an honest boundary is better than a test that pretends otherwise.

The mutation check (disabling a control and asserting the test fails) is run once per control during this ticket, and the results are recorded; it is not left running in CI.

## Test plan
The suite is the test plan. It runs per-PR on the trading paths and nightly in full. Failures are treated as release-blocking, in line with R3's Safety gate where "a failure blocks merge, not just release".

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification work. It must not itself introduce weakness: crafted-request fixtures must not contain real credentials, the ZAP configuration must be committed (so the scan is reproducible) and its findings triaged rather than baselined away.

## Accessibility notes
The SAST rule banning credential-shaped rendering must not be so broad that it blocks legitimate accessible labels; rules are written against field names and known shapes, not against arbitrary text. No control introduced here may be colour-only or pointer-only.

## Performance notes
The client-side rate limiting verified in the preview-spam case exists to protect budget #4: if preview traffic can starve the `entry` bucket, real orders slow down. The test asserts that real-order latency is unaffected while preview is spammed.

## Observability
Every abuse case asserts the expected audit row exists and is correctly attributed â€” an unauditable refusal is a finding. Metric `cv_ticket_guard_blocked_total{reason}` must increment for guard refusals.

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§2.2 requires, for any `security`-labelled Epic, that "STRIDE model finalized, findings triaged (fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off), sign-off comment from Security engineer". R3's gate adds "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes". This ticket is that close-out for the order ticket surface â€” and, because E31/E33/E34 inherit this Epic's intent layer, arm state and confirmation policy, signing it off is also signing off the foundation those Epics build on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Code review, security-focused**, of the shipped implementation: `packages/order-ticket-core` (idempotency-key derivation, error mapping, no credential handling), the arm store and `CMP-139` guard, the account/group selector's scope handling, the settings/defaults write path, the diagnostics rendering and its redaction, and the hotkey dispatcher's precedence order.
- **Verification that every Critical/High threat** from E30-X01 is closed: fixed with a test, or accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off and a residual-risk statement.
- **Audit-chain verification**: place, reject, arm, disarm, rebind a trading hotkey and change a trading default on demo, then verify each produced the expected audit entry with correct attribution, and that the chain hash-verifies (cross-checking E42's audit browser).
- **Client-only-control ledger**: an explicit written list of the controls that exist only on the client (hold-to-confirm, focus suppression, the visual environment distinction), each with its server-side counterpart named or its absence justified â€” handed to E43 as pen-test input.
- **Findings triage** with severity, owner and target; Critical/High closed before sign-off.
- **Sign-off comment** on this ticket and on the Epic, naming the reviewed commit shas.

## Out of scope
Fixing defects (they are filed against their owning Stories), backend OMS security sign-off (E29-X03), the R4 pen-test itself (E43), live-enablement gating (E44).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No Critical or High threat is open
  Then every Critical and High threat from E30-X01 is either verified closed by a test or accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off
Scenario: The audit trail is complete and attributable
  Given a placed order, a rejection, an arm, a disarm, a hotkey rebinding and a defaults change performed on demo
  Then each produced its expected audit entry with correct user, account and environment attribution, and the chain hash-verifies
Scenario: Client-only controls are documented, not assumed

Scenario: Sign-off is specific

```

## Technical notes / design
The review pays particular attention to three places where a plausible implementation would be subtly wrong: (1) the arm token being kept in any persistent store (it must be memory-only, and a restart must land in `locked`); (2) the guard being implemented as a hook that a call site can forget rather than a wrapper it cannot escape; (3) the diagnostics view redacting on render instead of relying on the server's redaction â€” the server must redact, and the client must additionally not log.

No new tests; this ticket verifies that the existing ones actually cover what they claim. Where they do not, a gap is filed against E30-X02 rather than being noted and forgotten.

This ticket is the security close-out. Standard: `04-security-program.md`; R3 Security gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4). Data classification: financial, account-scoped. Reviewed on demo only; no live credentials are used at any point.

The review confirms that no security control added late in the Epic broke the a11y contract â€” specifically that refusals are announced, that the guard's disabled state states a reason, and that nothing security-relevant is signalled by colour alone.
